_readme: Hand-reviewed transliteration aliases for duration-probe title resolution. This is the ONLY non-exact route into TRUTH: scripts/duration_probe_titles.py:resolve_exact() consults it, and scripts/duration_probe_cut.py uses it when a title has no exact skey match. Fuzzy matching is deliberately NOT allowed here, because a false merge relabels one work as another and the pool feeds truth ids. The relaxed consonant-skeleton key (cskel) exists for the opposite job -- disqualifying an OOC candidate -- where over-matching costs sample size and never validity.
_schema: <title as it appears in a filename or download_manifest file_title_raw>: {registry_id, status, evidence, reviewed_by, reviewed_on}. status must be 'accepted' to take effect; 'proposed' and 'rejected' are inert. evidence should name what was checked -- pallavi text, composer, raga -- not just that the strings look similar.
_status_2026_07_28: EMPTY, and correctly so. The rebuilt pool needs no aliases: the three transliteration cases the red team found (santanagopalakrishnam, alaipayuthey, chinnanchiru-kiliye) are all NEGATIVE-arm candidates, where the relaxed key disqualifies them without any truth claim. Add a row here only when a POOL title fails exact resolution and someone has verified the identity by hand.
